executiveSummary: Available reporting indicates a continued elevation of navigation integrity risks from GNSS interference and AIS manipulation globally, reinforced by new U.S. and U.K. government guidance to harden PNT-dependent maritime operations. Government Advisory Government Advisory

vendors: FURUNO - FA-50 Class B AIS transponder (discontinued; identity manipulation risk). Vendor
Port technology references from MARAD advisory - PRC-linked ship-to-shore cranes, LOGINK, Nuctech (risk categories, not confirmed incidents). MARAD
sectors: Ports and Terminal Operators (OT systems, cranes, logistics platforms)
Shipping Lines and Vessel Operators (bridge systems, AIS, GNSS-dependent navigation)

keyFindings: GNSS jamming and AIS manipulation remain globally impactful risks to maritime navigation, with updated MARAD and MCA guidance emphasizing multi-source position validation and incident reporting. MARAD Advisory UK MCA Notice

Vendor-confirmed AIS transponder vulnerability (FURUNO FA-50) enables onboard-network manipulation of vessel identification data; no patch available; upgrade or compensating controls required. Vendor Advisory

MARAD flagged cyber and national-security risks associated with certain foreign-manufactured port technologies, reinforcing the need for OT segmentation, vendor access control, and supply-chain scrutiny. MARAD Advisory
USCG NVIC 02-26 implementation guidance sets near-term compliance actions for vessels and port facilities, shaping cybersecurity program priorities into 2027. View Article

Unverified mass extortion claims against 38 maritime organizations highlight potential exposure via shared software or third-party providers, warranting monitoring and vendor-risk reviews. View Article

topThreats.title: 1) Port OT exposure tied to foreign-manufactured systems
topThreats.action: Strategic risk to port operations, logistics data, and national supply chains through embedded technology, vendor access, and data platforms.

topThreats.title: 2) Ongoing GNSS interference and AIS manipulation affecting navigation integrity
topThreats.action: Loss or corruption of PNT data can degrade route safety, increase collision/grounding risk, and impair VTS coordination.

topThreats.title: 3) FURUNO FA-50 AIS transponder vulnerability (no patch; identity manipulation risk)
topThreats.action: Onboard attackers could alter MMSI and AIS parameters, undermining vessel identification and traffic services.

topThreats.title: 4) USCG NVIC 02-26 cybersecurity implementation requirements
topThreats.action: Establishes near-term compliance obligations shaping cyber controls and staffing across U.S. maritime operations.

topThreats.title: 5) Unverified mass data-extortion claims against maritime firms
topThreats.action: Even if overstated, multi-tenant or shared software exposure could amplify incident scope across shipping, ports, and logistics.

descriptions: Navigation data manipulation: AIS track and identity tampering; GNSS spoofing causing false positions. Formal ATT&CK mapping not confirmed in sources.
Supply-chain and third-party exposure: Potential risks via foreign-manufactured port systems or shared logistics platforms (no specific intrusion TTPs confirmed).
Extortion dynamics: Data theft and coercion claims against multiple maritime organizations; intrusion vectors unspecified in current reporting.
Onboard lateral movement risk: FA-50 issue requires internal network access, underscoring the threat of local or bridged access to navigation VLANs.

outlook72h: Analysts should monitor for additional GNSS interference advisories and navigational anomaly reports in contested regions; the immediate risk to navigation integrity remains elevated but manageable with procedural controls. Confidence: Medium.
